title: Heesch numbers and maximal coronas of small polyforms with certificates and a Lean-verified SAT encoding
description: Article (version 2.1) with records, code and a Lean formalization. For a fixed selection of 3,964 shapes from Kaplan's tables of unmarked polyominoes, polyhexes and polyiamonds, every Heesch number Hc and Hh is given a corona witness (checked by two geometric checkers) and an upper-bound CNF whose unsatisfiability proof is accepted by drat-trim (5,019 proofs). A Lean 4 theorem proves the SAT encoding sound on the square, hexagonal and triangular grids (six statements, standard axioms, six kernel runs with five implementations), and a recorded finite comparison connects all 5,019 checked CNF files to the Lean definition; a second encoding agrees on every value. Maximal coronas of 22 shapes are counted by two implementations (complete agreement in 28 of 30 combinations), and a restricted search of 3,442 polyominoes with 20-28 cells yields no finite Hh=4 example. drat-trim and the file comparison are outside Lean; no human expert review.
